name: Tocharian A
catalog_citation: Malzahn, Melanie. 2010. The Tocharian Verbal System (Brill's Studies in Indo-European Languages & Linguistics 3). Leiden/Boston: Brill. Chapter 1 'Sound Laws', sec. 1.4 'Vowel Balance and Related Phenomena in Tocharian A', pp. 8-10. Secondary: Krause, Todd B.…
catalog_locator: Malzahn 2010 pp. 8-10 (sec. 1.4); LRC Tocharian Online lesson-10 page, Series Introduction sec. 1.4
catalog_quote: Whereas the location of the accent in Tocharian B can be detected on the basis of the different renderings of /ä/ and /a/, no such device is available for establishing the synchronic accent rules of Tocharian A. Consequently, there are different views on the synchronic accent of Tocharian A. However, most scholars work with the hypothesis that the accent rules of pre-Tocharian A at least were the same as the ones found valid for Tocharian B, i.e., that one can reconstruct the accent system of Proto-Tocharian on the basis of Tocharian B alone. ... Since in the context of vowel balance a full vowel never undergoes any kind of weakening in an initial syllable, it is rather safe to assume that in Tocharian A full vowels implementing the peak of an initial syllable in a word bore the accent.

sources.citation: Koller, Bernhard. 2015. Studies in Tocharian Phonology above the Word-Level. PhD dissertation, UCLA (218 pp.).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: p. 85: 'It appears that this enclitic [oki] was not necessarily unaccented, but could attract the accent of its host. However, due to the small number of attestations of this kind and our very limited knowledge of TA accent, the exact conditions and scope of this phenomenon have to remain in the dark for the time being.' p. 32 gives Vowel Balance as a pre-TA sound change (*ā > a, *a > ä after/between [-high] vowels), 'reanalyzed as a morphophonological process (Kim 2007: 12)' synchronically. TOC has 'Accent in TB' (1.1.3) but no TA word-accent section.

sources.quote: 'Kakie-libo ukazanija na sushchestvovanie v T.A.ja. v period ego pis'mennoj fiksacii udarenija i/ili tonal'nyx razlichij v pis'mennyx pamjatnikax otsutstvujut.' [Any indications of the existence of stress and/or tonal distinctions in Tocharian A in the period of its written attestation are absent from the written monuments.] Also p. 401: 'polnoudarnye slova ne mogut okanchivat'sja na a i ä' (fully-stressed words cannot end in a or ä).

sources.citation: Kim, Ronald I. 2007. Vowel Weakening in Tocharian A Preterite Participles and Abstract Nouns. Kyoto University Linguistic Research 26: 1-30.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: p. 9: 'Although we know little about TA accentuation, it seems probable that the position of stress played a role in this bifurcation: if we assume that primary stress fell on the first "full vowel" (see sec. 6)...'. p. 26: 'It is tempting to suppose that primary stress in pre-TA came to fall on the first full vowel, with secondary stress following two syllables after; thus the stress pattern in such forms was *V́ V V̀ ... The raising of *ā > *a after a primary stressed syllable, and further raising of *a > *ä between stressed syllables, would then be phonetically most natural.'
